ZUMA's LIFELINE

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Shots have been fired from within the ANC, yet President Zuma has avoided the attack - but for how long?

Unique Selling Point:
NEWS OF THE WEEK

Summary:
The ANC's NEC deliberated on Zuma's fate following a “surprise” motion by Hanekom on Saturday that the party’s highest decision-making body recalls the president or that he steps down.

President Zuma survived - but at what cost?




Further information:
After surviving an unparalleled attack on his leadership of the ANC, a defiant President Jacob Zuma has told the party's national executive committee (NEC) that stepping down would be like handing himself over to the enemy and he would never do it.

Zuma addressed the NEC following a grueling three-day battle over his future, initiated by Tourism Minister Derek Hanekom. The meeting, scheduled to end on Sunday, was extended to Monday as opposing sides failed to reach consensus.

We speak to Prince Mashele, Karima Brown, Sipho Pityana - Filmed Gwede Mantashe at the Presser on Tuesday and hopefully also a pro-Zuma person - ideally Jesse Duarte.

The idea is to do a quick recap of the blow the President suffered this year and the way forward.

Press Release:


Zuma Lifeline
A party at war with itself? President Zuma’s leadership was this week, for the first time, openly challenged from within the ANC. In an unprecedented move, members of the ANC’s National Executive Committee debated a motion of no confidence, supported by party heavyweights. Carte Blanche asks: though the motion ultimately failed, what will the impact of this body blow to President Jacob Zuma be?


Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: In an unexpected move, calls for President Jacob Zuma to step down came from INSIDE the ANC’s highest decision making body - the National Executive Committee.

KARIMA: The African National Congress is right down the middle, I think it is deeply divided - it is at war with itself.

VO: Rumours of blistering debates, ministers nearly exchanging blows and turning on each other in defence of, or against, President Zuma - dominated the headlines this week - some saying the countdown for Zuma’s exit has begun….

LINK: Calls for President Zuma to go are not all new – but for the first time it is his own comrades that are speaking out FRIENDS LINK

MBEKI: JZ is a very smart political operator – he is no push over – so those who are plotting against him they have to be smarter than him. MBEKI9

VO: The challengers were not… the bid failed and Jacob Zuma survived the call for his removal - emerging with the support of the NEC

UPSOUND GWEDE: We confirmed him as president of ANC & the president of the Republic. [04:48-05:40] (clip 0011KE)

VO: But not without battle wounds says Political Analyst Prince Mashele.

PRINCE: if you look at it from the perspective of the organisation that he represents – he actually has not won because he has killed the ANC. INT1

VO: The significance of the internal motion cannot be ignored says Sipho Pityana, ANC Stalwart and convener of the Save South Africa Movement.

PITYANA: It is a culmination, it is an acknowledgement by ANC leadership// that we have a serious political problem in the leadership of JZ.

VO: Traditionally the NEC has been a safe space for the president says 702 Political Commentator Karima Brown.

KARIMA: no one would have thought that ANC leaders // would even ventured this kind of discussion //. INT1 M6

VO: But ANC’s Gwede Mantashe says it’s a discussion that became necessary.

UPSOUND GWEDE: THE NEC TOOK TIME ELABORATE PREVIOUSLY identified negative narrative against the President… time to unpack that idea.

VO: Tourism Minister Derek Hanekom, who also heads the ANC’s Disciplinary Committee kick started a no confidence debate at the ANC’s National Executive Committee last week.

It was a courageous move that was backed by several other ministers including Aaron Motsoaledi and Thulas Nxesi.

CUT END KARIMA: This is where people slug it out – many of it happens in his absence – this happened to his face – every single member of NEC given opportunity to speak // INT1 M8

VO: Mantashe insists there is no hierarchy in the NEC – members are equals and despite a call for a secret vote on the President’s fate – that is simply not how it is done.

UPSOUND GWEDE: NEC OF THE ANC DON’t VOTE on any issue // the persuade each other on everything to a point of consensus no matter how difficult.

VO: But for some speaking out against Number One was extremely difficult.

BONGANI: RUMOURS THAT PEOPLE WERE SHAKING WHEN THEY SPOKE
PRINCE: you shake because you know this man pulls the levers of power that determine your life – that is what makes people shake INT1 M3

VO: The President’s supporters did not hesitate to discredit his critics says Karima.

KARIMA: Many of them argued people serving pro-opposition agenda – agents of regime change – CIA agents – counter revolutionaries INT1 M9

VO: But what happens now to the members that were brave enough to criticise their Number One? Because outside of the NEC they are not just members – they hold powerful positions as ministers.

Political Economist Moelesti Mbeki believes President Zuma still holds a very strong hand.

MBEKI: I don’t expect JZ is going to take this one lying down – I think he is going to punish somebody. MBEKI7

VO: Deputy Secretary General Jessie Duarte attempted to diffuse the situation.

UPSOUND JESSE DUARTE: Contestation comment [09:48-10:15](Clip 0013YM)
UPSOUND JESSE DUARTE: Don't expect mass resignations[11:25-11:52] (Clip0013YM)

BONGANI: What is he fires them?
PRINCE: IF he fires them he is actually building an anti- zuma army outside the structures of the ANC and outside his cabinet – so it is in his interest to keep them there – even though he doesn’t trust them and they don’t trust him – // INT1 M15//–

VO: And the cracks are starting to show, with resistance building from within says Karima.

KARIMA: If you listen to the words chosen by leaders of ANc to describe meeting – robust, painful discussion – people didn’t hold back – INT1 M8

VO: The ANC’s KZN region, came out in full support of President Zuma – they were surprised by the no confidence motion at the NEC, says spokesman Mdumiseni Ntuli.

NTULI: We were very worried – the national executive committee will not allow – it was contrary to the traditions of the movement – it would also have been completely unconstitutional. INT1 M1

LINK: Perhaps no other political party prides itself in its traditions and discipline than the ANC – decisions are made by the collective and all members must tow the line – but with a direct challenge to President Zuma’s authority has the ground shifted. SHIFT LINK

VO: The President would like South Africans to believe that an external enemy is at work – claiming there “was a sinister plot to discredit him and remove from office driven by Western Powers working through various parties and organisations in South Africa.”

LINK: In 2016 has a taken a lot of blows, time after time he’s been against the ropes and yet his opponents have not been able to knock him out // BOXING LINK

VO It’s been a big year for the President starting with Nenegate costing the country in the region of R500 BILLION rand as we kicked off 2016.

• Then the Constitutional Court ruling in the Public Protector’s Nkandla Report Case in March – ordered the president to pay back the money for non-security upgrades.

• And then the Pretoria High Court found that the 2009 decision to drop 783 corruption charges against President Zuma was in fact irrational and he should face them.

• But then in August, the ANC took a knock when it lost power in the three major metros – Tshwane, Johannesburg and Nelson Mandela Bay.

This, was first tipping point says Moeletsi.

MBEKI: // many people in the ANC didn’t think the Zuma’s action would affect the huge number of people voting for the ANC.

VO: Events kept snowballing with the state capture report in November, and then another vote of no confidence attempt in parliament – but the biggest blow came from the ANC Stalwarts.

MBEKI: The real trigger is that the old guard of the ANC has now become organized within the ANC and it is demanding that certain changes introduced. MBEKI1

VO: But the ANC leadership is adamant about projecting a united front…

UPSOUND GWEDE: The NEC resolved working towards unity movement" [15:46-16:42] (clip 0013YM)

LINK: With slow economic growth, unemployment and downgrades by rating agencies – all indications are there are tough times ahead for South aFricans and for all our intrigue about what happens next in the ANC succession battle is it really about what is best for the country? COUNTRY LINK

PITYANA: We actually are having the most unprecedented dis-functionality here – the state not capable to implement the kinds of reforms that we need to ensure that South Africa succeeds in a difficult economic and political environment.

KARIMA: Zuma is not the sum total of what is wrong with the ANC – the ANC problems deep rooted. INT1 M22

VO: But solutions won’t come overnight says Mantashe.

UPSOUND GWEDE: *introspection is a process not an event [17:11-17:21](clip00167)

VO: A process that might cost the ANC their political clout.

KARIMA: Scandals come out day after day // this is bad news for brand ANC INT1 M17


VO: The national executive committee calls the shots in the ANC – it has the power to recall Jacob Zuma. But that seems unlikely says Prince with the committee’s unwavering support for the President.

PRINCE: // the NEC has adopted a collective decision to defend that which Zuma represents – it closes the chapter – we now know it is official that the ANC defends corruption. INT 1 M1

VO: It’s a theory, Mdumiseni from the ANC KZN branch denies.

NTULI: We do not condone wrong doings – we believe first and foremost – the allegations – the president is not in court – he is not charged.. INT1 M6


PITYANA: At the heart of the problem is a political mismanagement and the political crisis, // – his continued leadership of the country is harmful to the economy and the stability of the country.

MBEKI: Their polcies are going to lead to their loss of power by the ANC - trying to scapegoat JZ instead of solving the bigger problem will not stop the ANC from losing power. MBEKI5




PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: In a historic event – the ANC National Executive Committee – debated a call for President Zuma to step down.

KARIMA: No one would have thought that ANC leaders // would even ventured this kind of discussion //.

VO: What will the repercussions be?

PROMO 2
VO: President Zuma survived a challenge from inside the ANC – but is it a victory?

PRINCE: – he actually has not won because he has killed the ANC

PROMO 3
VO: With calls for President Zuma to step down from inside the ANC – it seem that he is losing ground.

PITYANA: There is a strong feeling that ZUma is costing the ANC its standing .

VO: is this the tipping point?
